newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa ends tightly mixed, awaits news.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa ends tightly mixed, awaits news.

text.p: LIFFE cocoa futures ended another lacklustre session tightly mixed as participants remained sidelined awaiting significant crop or grind news, traders said.
"The market is quite dead," said one trader.
"It's just been a waste of time," said another. "It has been a quiet week."
Traders in New York noted a round of arbitrage buying in New York against London due to higher sterling against the U.S. dollar, driving the sterling-denominated London cocoa lower.
Market participants in London had hoped pre-weekend trading would stir interest and boost prices following two straight good finishes for the last two Fridays.
"At the moment, we don't really see anything on the horizon that's going to stir it up," he said.
By the finish, most-active December shed one stg to 982 stg a tonne after rising earlier to the day's high of 988 on light trade buying.
Barring major developments, traders expect the market to hover within the immediate 980-950 stg range.
Overall volume was a modest 3,259 lots.

On the fundamental front, Brazil said Bahia cocoa arrivals were 209,329 bags in the week ending September 15 compared to 25,729 bags in the previous week and 28,066 bags in the corresponding week last year.
This brought total arrivals for the 1996/97 crop to 1,643,435 bags.
Technically, analysts said the London December cocoa was likely to try to extend its recent gains but any sustained move above the closely-watched 1,000 stg hurdle would demand time.
